Those are probably the three biggest existential crises that humans face right now.

If I had to categorize them it would be:

  • The cosmic flyswatter - Meteors, gamma ray bursts, other similarly catastrophic celestial events which are rather common and could easily destroy us. Unless we can colonize other star systems, we won't be fully 'proof' from these types of events.
  • Man-made crises - including AI, environmental degradation, grey goo, superbugs, etc. These types of events can chase us, so to speak, and are a bit harder to deal with than simply leaving the local cluster.
  • Time - the ultimate road block is time (technically entropy) and the inevitable heat death of the universe. This is the upper-bound of human longevity as we currently see it. Stars expanding and consuming nearby planets, exploding in a supernova, or guttering out into a glowing ball of heavy elements. Our present understanding of physics pegs this as beyond our ability to do anything about.

Back to the point, we can solve those first two problems by spreading our species across the stars to some extent. The exception being that certain man-made problems could well reshape the entire universe (for example, a hostile super-intelligence) and bear special consideration.
